title: Balancing engineering quality, deadline and cost

videos.script: Helena wants a feature by the end of the quarter. Sílvio wants it to cost less. The team wants to build it properly. {{title}} The classic picture is a triangle. Scope, time and cost, and fixing two moves the third. Quality is often drawn in the middle, as if it could be cut to hit a date. {{triangle}} This lesson argues that internal quality is the wrong thing to cut. Code that is hard to change makes every next feature slower. And the point where that catches up with you comes in weeks, not months. {{stamina}} Then a date nobody can move. The tax authority publishes a new layout for the CT-e, with a day after which the old one is refused. {{cte}} The date is fixed. The team is the team. So the thing that moves is scope. {{scope}} Renata takes three options to Tomás, Helena and Sílvio. Each one has a cost, a time and a risk. {{options}} The business chooses. Renata's job is to make the consequences plain, and to write down the debt they agree to carry. {{debt}}
